content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Cloud CDN: Content Delivery Network on Google Cloud"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Cloud CDN (Content Delivery Network) uses Google's globally distributed edge points of presence to cache HTTP(S) load balanced content close to your users. Caching content at the edge of Google's network provides faster content delivery while reducing serving costs."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Benefits of Using Cloud CDN"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Improved Website Performance: By caching content closer to users, Cloud CDN reduces latency and improves website loading times."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Reduced Bandwidth Costs: Caching frequently accessed content reduces the load on your origin servers, resulting in lower bandwidth costs."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Enhanced Scalability: Cloud CDN helps your website handle traffic spikes by serving content from the cache, preventing your origin servers from being overwhelmed."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Global Reach: Google's extensive network of edge locations ensures that your content is delivered quickly and reliably to users around the world."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"How Cloud CDN Works"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"When a user requests content from your website, Cloud CDN checks its cache to see if the content is available. If the content is cached, Cloud CDN serves it directly to the user. If the content is not cached, Cloud CDN retrieves it from your origin server and caches it for future requests. The origin server can be a Compute Engine instance, a Cloud Storage bucket, or any other HTTP(S) server."},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Setting Up Cloud CDN"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before you can use Cloud CDN, you need to have a load balancer configured. Cloud CDN works with HTTP(S) Load Balancing. Here's a general outline of the steps involved:"},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Configure an HTTP(S) Load Balancer: Set up a load balancer to distribute traffic to your backend services or buckets."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Enable Cloud CDN: Enable Cloud CDN on the backend service or bucket that you want to cache."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Configure Cache Settings: Configure cache settings, such as the cache TTL (Time To Live), to control how long content is cached."},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Example: Enabling Cloud CDN for a Backend Service"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can enable Cloud CDN for a backend service using the Google Cloud Console or the gcloud command-line tool."},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"# Using gcloud command-line tool\ngcloud compute backend-services update <backend-service-name> --global --enable-cdn"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"Replace <backend-service-name> with the name of your backend service."},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Cache Invalidation"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"Sometimes, you may need to invalidate cached content to ensure that users receive the latest version. You can invalidate cached content using the gcloud command-line tool or the Cloud CDN API."},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"# Using gcloud to invalidate a cache entry\ngcloud compute url-maps invalidate-cdn-cache <url-map-name> --path=\"/path/to/invalidate\" --global"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"Replace <url-map-name> with the name of your URL map and \"/path/to/invalidate\" with the path to the content you want to invalidate."},{"order":23,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices"},{"order":24,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Set appropriate cache TTLs: Configure cache TTLs based on how frequently your content changes. Longer TTLs reduce origin server load, but may result in users seeing stale content."},{"order":25,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use cache keys effectively: Use cache keys to differentiate between different versions of your content. For example, you can use query parameters to create different cache keys for different versions of an image."},{"order":26,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Monitor cache hit ratio: Monitor your cache hit ratio to ensure that your content is being cached effectively. A low cache hit ratio may indicate that your cache settings need to be adjusted."},{"order":27,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":28,"type":"paragraph","text":"Cloud CDN is a powerful tool for improving website performance, reducing bandwidth costs, and enhancing scalability. By caching content closer to users, Cloud CDN helps you deliver a better user experience and reduce the load on your origin servers. By following the best practices outlined in this tutorial, you can effectively use Cloud CDN to optimize your website's performance."}]
